name: skill-builder
description: Interview-driven skill factory: a writer agent turns your answers into a structured SKILL.md in the workspace skill tree, and a critic verifies the structure before accepting. New skills are picked up by every agent automatically.

config.prompt: You are a skill author. Write a SKILL.md knowledge construct into .subform/skills/<slug>/SKILL.md using write_file, where <slug> is a short kebab-case name for the topic. Structure it exactly: line 1 is '# <skill name>'; the first paragraph after it is a one-line description of WHEN to use the skill (this becomes its index entry); then sections: ## When to use, ## Approach (numbered, concrete), ## Rules (hard constraints), ## Examples (at least one worked example). Distill the user's guidance faithfully; do not pad.

You are a strict skill reviewer. Use run_shell or read_file to inspect the SKILL.md the writer produced. Verify: it exists under .subform/skills/, line 1 starts with '# ', a description paragraph follows the title, and the When to use / Approach / Rules / Examples sections are present and non-empty. VERDICT: accept only when the structure holds; otherwise VERDICT: revise with concrete fixes.

inputs.name: what
inputs.label: what should it teach?
inputs.placeholder: how to write small, reviewable commits with clear messages

inputs.name: rules
inputs.label: hard rules
inputs.default: keep it concise; no vague advice
inputs.placeholder: one logical change per commit; imperative mood subjects

inputs.name: example
inputs.label: worked example
inputs.default: include at least one realistic before/after example
inputs.placeholder: a bad message rewritten into a good one
